title: Embed/rerank compatibility: Link-header pagination, idempotency & HTTP error alignment
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Multiple internal and third-party clients rely on legacy embeddings + rerank endpoints with cursor-based pagination and a mix of semantics (Link header vs cursor in body). Recent changes introduced subtle incompatibilities: inconsistent Link header formats, different HTTP status mapping for partial failures, and lack of idempotency semantics for rerank POSTs leading to duplicate scoring on retries. Scope: deliver a compatibility layer that normalizes pagination to a Link-header-first model with clear fallback to body cursors, define a strict HTTP error mapping and retry guidance, and add optional idempotency tokens to rerank requests so client SDKs can safely retry without duplicate scoring. This ticket coordinates the PM spec, acceptance criteria, SDK guidance, and rollout plan.
proposed_solution: Ship a compatibility adapter in the API gateway that: 1) Always emits RFC-5988 style Link headers for paging (rel=next, rel=prev) when result sets are paginated, with a stable opaque cursor token in the query param; 2) Includes an explicit "cursor" field in the response body for legacy clients that expect it; 3) Normalizes HTTP error codes: map internal transient failures to 503 with Retry-After, user/client input errors to 400/422, authentication to 401/403, and 429 for rate limits; 4) Accepts an optional Idempotency-Key header on rerank POSTs and de-duplicates scoring within a 5 minute window; 5) For streaming embed responses, emit a final non-streamed metadata chunk containing the same Link header and cursor fields to ensure parity for clients that switch between streaming and non-streaming modes.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway emits RFC-5988 Link headers with rel=next and rel=prev for paginated responses
Response body continues to include 'cursor' field for backward compatibility
HTTP error mapping documented and put behind compatibility flag; tests cover mappings and Retry-After behavior
Idempotency-Key accepted for rerank POSTs; duplicate requests with same key return stored result without re-scoring
Streaming and non-streaming paths produce identical final pagination metadata
SDK tests updated to demonstrate safe retries using Idempotency-Key
Performance regression <= 3% p99 latency for common embed/rerank requests when adapter enabled
tradeoffs: Centralizing normalization at the gateway avoids changing many downstream services but adds runtime overhead and complexity to routing. Idempotency window (5 minutes) is a balance between storage cost and duplicate avoidance; long windows increase storage and edge cases, short windows risk duplicate scoring. Keeping both Link header and body cursor increases response size but preserves client compatibility.
testing_plan: Unit tests in adapter for Link header formatting and cursor encoding/decoding
Integration tests: legacy SDKs (v1.2) and new SDKs against compatibility flag on/off
Chaos test: simulate transient failures and assert 503+Retry-After mapping and client retry behavior
Load test: measure added p99 latency and CPU overhead at gateway at production-like QPS
Security review: validate Idempotency-Key header cannot be used to leak cached results across tenants
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy to staging; 2) Run integration suite with legacy SDKs and internal apps for 48h; 3) Canary to 5% of production traffic with detailed telemetry on pagination headers and idempotency hits; 4) Gradual ramp to 100% in 24-72h if no regressions; 5) Deprecation announcement for legacy-only cursor-only responses after 90 days.
open_questions: Should the compatibility adapter sign/verify cursors to avoid replay across regions?
Edge case: how should cursor tokens interact with model variant fallbacks (when a different model returns fewer items)?
What metrics should we expose to customers to show when adapter is active for their requests?
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created by Ava Chen. Initial proposal drafted, linked ENG dependency ENG-48210.
2026-03-02: Design sync with SDK leads (Sofia Patel) — agreed to expose Idempotency-Key in all official SDKs and add helper retry wrappers.
2026-03-03: Engineering spike (ENG-48210) shows cursor signing feasible with <1% p99 overhead; noted cross-region key rotation concerns.
2026-03-04: PM review with Compliance (Jordan Lee) — no additional compliance controls required but audit logs must include idempotency key usage for 30 days.
2026-03-05: Draft spec posted to Confluence and PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/289
notes_for_engineering: Please implement feature flag 'compat.embed_rerank.link_headers_v1' to allow fast rollback. Adapter must attach the following headers: Link, X-Compat-Version:1, and preserve any upstream Retry-After. Use tenant-scoped idempotency key cache with TTL=300s. Ensure cursor tokens are opaque base64 + HMAC signed using gateway key rotation pipeline.
notes_for_design: UX doc: SDK retry helper should default to using Idempotency-Key and expose a 'retry_policy' argument. Console should surface when a request used compatibility adapter and show the cursor token in raw response view for debugging.
